findings.title: A modular workspace still has a large coupled session engine
findings.observed: The archive has 28 actual workspace members. The engine manifest depends on catalog, RAW, GPU, pipeline and other domain crates; mandatory faces and denoise-core dependencies coexist with optional neural denoise/SAM. Engine source is 44,872 physical lines. Taking the entire engine would bring independent catalog, session and model-feature authority into Studio.
findings.risk: A renamed all-in-one Studio facade would preserve rebuild coupling and duplicate Handshake ownership.
proposed_controls: Extract candidate non-AI leaf crates behind explicit input/output contracts.
Keep CKC catalog/CAS ownership and shared Handshake document/session authority.
Measure actual dependency-closed compilation separately; LOC and member count do not prove build speed.
findings.proof_required: Fresh modular build graph, dependency feature closure and ARM-host/x64-target proofs in the authorized implementation session.

findings.title: RAW input coverage includes preview-only and profile approximation paths
findings.observed: RAW decoding dispatches many vendor containers, but unsupported variants can return a camera JPEG preview explicitly marked preview-only. Preview development chooses binned or bilinear/AHD paths; full sensor normalization applies black correction, CFA crop and DNG opcodes. Non-DNG camera matrix fallback and supported variant limits require fixtures.
findings.risk: A successful open can be mistaken for full-fidelity editable RAW support.
proposed_controls: Expose preview-only versus sensor-developed state, source codec, camera/profile and unsupported settings in document receipts and Argus.
Test each required camera/container/process variant with full sensor development against independent reference output.
Preserve original source bytes and version conversion assumptions.
findings.proof_required: Installed Lightroom/Camera Raw differential renders, profile/crop/orientation/highlight tests and original-byte retention; NOT_RUN in this lane.

findings.title: Read-only Lightroom catalog scope now has a narrow operator approval
findings.observed: The candidate reader is a pure Rust SQLite file/page parser, not an SQL engine, and consumes .lrcat plus committed WAL. Current inspected v02.206 prohibits SQLite use including imports. Fresh session.json records STUDIO-APPROVAL-LRCAT permitting read-only .lrcat parsing, without SQL engine, query interface, writable catalog or second database, with sole SurrealDB/EventLedger authority.
findings.risk: Adoption before root propagates the precise approved exception would conflict with the current spec; a broad exception would create a second database authority.
proposed_controls: Root-owned spec enrichment must carry the exact approved read-only external file-format boundary.
Preserve full catalog migration scope; XMP alone is not equivalent.
Route normalized imported state into CKC/SurrealDB/EventLedger and never expose SQL/query/write catalog behavior.
findings.proof_required: Read the final current spec and contract before implementation. No additional operator approval is requested by this report.

findings.title: Catalog migration does not recreate all Lightroom editing history or collection behavior
findings.observed: The reader maps master images, virtual copies, settings/XMP, ratings, pick state, keywords and collection membership. Develop history and snapshots remain archive data instead of native undo/develop histories; smart collections become current-membership albums with rules archived. The archive omits BLOB values, can skip content at 32 MiB, and has total retention limits.
findings.risk: A conversion can appear complete while losing executable rules, edit history, opaque records or oversized archive provenance.
proposed_controls: Create field-level imported/transformed/archived/unsupported/missing conversion receipts.
Keep source catalog and original media as retained provenance independent of a lossy candidate archive.
Implement native history/snapshot/rule semantics required by the full user catalog workflow rather than treating archived text as parity.
findings.proof_required: Real original-app catalogs covering virtual copies, snapshots, historic process versions, smart rules, offline media, duplicate paths, BLOB/oversize data and recovery; NOT_RUN.

findings.title: Catalog reader has parser budgets but cancellation and snapshot proof are partial
findings.observed: Catalog and WAL are loaded into vectors with file length/mtime checked before and after. Committed WAL frame checksum/salt/page validation exists. The page parser limits columns, rows, payload bytes, overflow traversal and B-tree depth, but the inspected inner row traversal has no cancellation token; outer table checks provide coarser cancellation.
findings.risk: Large/adversarial files can delay cancellation; length/mtime stability does not alone establish a content snapshot during concurrent writes.
proposed_controls: Carry cancellation/deadline through page, cell, overflow and row work.
Apply aggregate byte admission before allocation and bound decompression/catalog record expansion.
Use a captured content identity and stable snapshot protocol; reject concurrent source changes and incomplete WAL state with a recoverable receipt.
findings.proof_required: Corrupt/truncated/WAL-race/oversize inputs, cancel at nested parser boundaries and byte-pressure fixtures, preserving source files.

findings.title: Prepared catalog application has useful identity checks, while editing uses shared selection
findings.observed: Lightroom import preparation captures library identity; owner application rejects cancellation or a reopened library, even at the same path. In contrast, develop auto-sync and model instructions use active photo/shared selection, and most MCP editing tools require activating the target first.
findings.risk: Parallel models can target another actor's active selection or time/context without an OS-level data race.
proposed_controls: Reuse prepared-input/owner-apply separation with explicit document/object identifiers.
Require actor/job identity, expected revision, touched-object set and structured conflict result on mutation.
Give each actor its own context and Argus snapshot stream; common UI assets expose explicit targets rather than relying on shared activation.
findings.proof_required: Interleaved human plus multiple-agent edits, reopened document, cancelled prepared operation and disjoint/conflicting target tests.

findings.title: Applied edits, durable journal and XMP writes have distinct failure states
findings.observed: Command execution persists pending operations after applying in memory and can return NotSaved. Journal append carries CRC/sequence recovery; snapshot writes use temporary file, sync and rename. XMP auto-write errors are logged as warnings. File lock contention rejects opening, but other file-open/lock errors permit an unprotected library with a warning.
findings.risk: The operator/model can confuse visible edit success with durable save or accidentally write an unprotected store.
proposed_controls: Expose applied/durable/exported revision separately in one receipt and visible state.
Do not adopt candidate catalog persistence as a second authority; integrate CKC durability transactions.
Fail closed for write ownership, or expose an explicit read-only recovery mode when locking is unavailable.
Make sidecar failure attributable and retriable without corrupting original or owned foreign XML fields.
findings.proof_required: Disk-full/permission/short-append/lock-unavailable/crash/reopen/sidecar retry tests through the owned production boundary.

findings.title: High-depth and GPU paths are different execution surfaces
findings.observed: The documented pipeline uses scene-linear Rec.2020. GPU render declines non-U8 output and several proof/LUT/mask cases. CPU render has separate U16/F32 finish and deep export profile/metadata routes.
findings.risk: Preview equivalence can hide deep export, profile, soft-proof and clipping errors.
proposed_controls: Record chosen backend, working/output space, bit depth, profile, fallback reason and render identity.
Test display preview and exported high-depth/print delivery independently.
Share one color contract with other Studio assets and preserve unclipped linear data where the workflow requires it.
findings.proof_required: GPU/CPU plus installed-original differential checks across wide gamut, HDR, ICC soft-proof and deep export; NOT_RUN.

findings.title: Soft memory gate is not cancellable bounded admission
findings.observed: WorkGate holds used/limit under Mutex and Condvar. It waits only when there is an existing holder; one oversized sole holder is allowed. acquire_urgent adds bytes without waiting. acquire has no cancellation/deadline/fairness parameter. Transfer workers are clamped to 1–8, but DNG admission can block before its next cancellation check.
findings.risk: Swarm requests can exceed aggregate bytes or remain parked after cancellation; notify_all can cause repeated contention.
proposed_controls: Use bounded byte/job admission with explicit overload, cancellation, deadline and fairness outcomes.
Reserve memory before large source/decoder allocation and cap bypass lanes.
Use owner actors and message passing for mutations; restrict synchronization to short budget/cache transitions.
Expose queued/running/reserved bytes, pressure cause and cancellation latency through diagnostics.
findings.proof_required: Sustained multi-agent mixed-size import/render/thumbnail jobs, oversized single jobs, urgent work saturation and cancel-under-pressure.

findings.title: Existing tests prove narrow internal behavior rather than Lightroom workflow parity
findings.observed: GPU equivalence compares the candidate CPU path with U8 tolerances and returns without testing when no adapter is available. Crop tests include synthetic round-trips and two real-export dimension examples, not full pixel or document comparisons. The parity document includes feature/control existence assertions and explicitly leaves a side-by-side Lightroom fidelity suite unfinished.
findings.risk: Feature names, internal reference agreement or skipped hardware runs are mistaken for professional parity.
proposed_controls: Separate enumerated, statically traced, executed, skipped and independently compared coverage.
Build original-app workflow fixtures with pixel/color/document loss oracles and recoverability.
Require an explicit unavailable/skipped verdict for missing adapters/codecs, not a parity success.
findings.proof_required: Independent installed-Lightroom proofs are all NOT_RUN in this lane.

findings.title: EffectCraft has 36 members but a coupled host/session facade
findings.observed: The workspace is split into render/effects/time/keyframe/expr/media/codec/parser/UI members. Engine source is 60,853 physical lines and the UI is 45,915; mandatory segmentation remains in the engine manifest. Reusing the entire project/engine/desktop application would bring a separate document, file format, editor state and task system.
findings.risk: A Studio sub-application duplicates common authority and retains expensive facade dependency closure.
proposed_controls: Adopt or adapt independently testable classical engine leaves.
Use shared native document, CKC persistence, common parameterized UI assets and kernel diagnostics adapters.
Exclude model-powered segmentation from this non-AI scope without excluding classical masking/tracking/retouching.
findings.proof_required: Actual feature-resolved build and ownership graphs before adoption; no build-speed claim from static counts.

findings.title: FilmCraft dependency source is pinned outside the EffectCraft archive
findings.observed: Cargo.lock contains 26 FilmCraft git package records at revision 2c5ba7a72619935f0481f99d59409e0d1844b234. Root dependency declarations use this pin. The separately retained current FilmCraft source uses 7b6c134 as a different revision; this EffectCraft archive does not contain the old FilmCraft source.
findings.risk: A current FilmCraft audit cannot prove the old dependency APIs, parsers or codec behavior required by this EffectCraft pin.
proposed_controls: Acquire and review the exact old git dependency if selecting this revision, or explicitly reconcile and repin with compatibility tests.
Select one shared media/interchange/codec ownership boundary across Studio.
Record lock/source pin closure and avoid silently substituting a newer implementation.
findings.proof_required: Dependency source at exact 2c5ba7a... is NOT_ACQUIRED by this lane; API/behavior divergence remains NOT_INSPECTED.

findings.title: Tick resolution matches the required constant but conversion semantics need hardening
findings.observed: Time uses i64 ticks at 254,016,000,000 per second with i128 arithmetic intermediates. Float-to-tick conversion rounds and clamps; NaN becomes zero. A zero rational divisor is coerced to one. Keyframe and remap paths derive f64 seconds.
findings.risk: Malformed rates or extreme durations can silently become valid-looking times; f64 interpolation can lose distinctions at long durations.
proposed_controls: Keep the existing required tick constant; do not invent an i128 persistence mandate.
Define typed invalid/non-finite/rate/range outcomes at import and command boundaries.
Test rational cadence, subframe values, reverse/stretch/remap, long duration and round-trip persistence.
findings.proof_required: Independent timing/frame-index/keyframe/easing fixtures across original-app and delivery formats.

findings.title: Single editor history and implicit time require actor-scoped adaptation
findings.observed: Session.edit clones the project and editor state, synchronizes dependent state, records whole-project history and publishes a new Arc. Commands can target explicit UIDs, but property mutation uses the shared editor time. Merge keys and editor state are session-wide in the inspected boundary.
findings.risk: Concurrent actors can cause logical target/time/history conflicts even if mutation is serialized by one owner.
proposed_controls: Require explicit time, target identifiers and expected revision for model commands.
Use one document mutation owner with conflict-aware transactions and actor-specific undo scopes.
Allow parallel immutable render/evaluation snapshots and receipts rather than large shared mutable locks.
findings.proof_required: Multiple actors editing at different times, stale snapshots, history grouping, cancellation before commit and deterministic replay.

findings.title: Native EC project routes do not establish Adobe project support or opaque preservation
findings.observed: File commands parse EC JSON or EC XML wrappers. Serialization performs a parse-back preflight and rejects a future schema. The loader warns that fields from a newer savedBy version can be lost on save. The inspected Services defaults access ambient directories/filesystem for methods beyond read/write.
findings.risk: Unknown fields are discarded and a partial capability adapter can still permit ambient access; EC XML could be misrepresented as Adobe AEPX.
proposed_controls: Keep a Handshake native document envelope with opaque/source provenance preservation and explicit conversion-loss receipts.
Implement genuine Adobe file adapters only after inspecting actual formats/resources and original-app fixtures.
Override the full filesystem/service interface under Handshake capability authority.
findings.proof_required: Unknown-field/schema round-trips, sandbox escape probes and native AEP/AEPX import/edit/conversion cases; NOT_RUN.

findings.title: Fallback output needs to carry fidelity state
findings.observed: Renderer returns a blank canvas above its nested depth threshold of 16, filters out unknown effect identifiers, and substitutes keyframed values when expression evaluation fails. Separate expr_tools commands already expose expression errors with comp/layer/property identity.
findings.risk: An image can look plausible while unsupported effects, nesting or expressions were not evaluated.
proposed_controls: Retain existing expression diagnostics and attach structured fallback/unsupported events to every render receipt.
Expose partial/incomplete output explicitly in Argus, export results and manual recovery paths.
Preserve unknown effect data in the native document even when it cannot yet render.
findings.proof_required: Unknown effects, recursive/deep comps, expression failure and missing/proxy footage must produce attributable recovery states.

findings.title: Expression runtime has local limits but no inspected job cancellation boundary
findings.observed: Expression evaluation limits nested frames and host-request passes; Boa sets loop iteration limit to 10 million and recursion limit to 400. Compiled scripts and runtime are cached per thread. The inspected evaluation interface has no job cancellation token/deadline parameter.
findings.risk: Many expression jobs can consume aggregate CPU/memory despite per-evaluation loop limits, and cancelled work can persist until a local budget is exhausted.
proposed_controls: Carry deadline/cancel/resource budget from job admission into expression execution.
Bound per-actor and aggregate compiled-script/runtime memory.
Use isolated immutable request context and typed timeout/cancel/error receipts.
findings.proof_required: Looping/recursive/host-request expressions, script cache growth, many actors and cancellation during evaluation.

findings.title: Unsupported OCIO transforms use identity and path caching can become stale
findings.observed: Unsupported transform application returns the input color. The code enumerates unsupported/missing file transforms. A global Mutex HashMap caches parsed configuration by string path or text, including None; the inspected cache function does not rehash a changed file at the same path.
findings.risk: Missing/unsupported or later-repaired configurations can yield plausible untransformed output or stale failure state.
proposed_controls: Make transform completeness and missing resources part of render/export state.
Key configuration/LUT dependencies by captured content identity and working/display/output space.
Reuse one Studio color authority, with recovery after resource replacement.
findings.proof_required: Unsupported transforms, external LUT changes at the same path, missing-then-repaired resources and original-app color pipeline comparisons.

findings.title: Timeline interchange is an approximate adapter, not native Premiere project parsing
findings.observed: The interchange crate documents FCP7 XML/FCPXML/OTIO/EDL/AAF/OMF support, no native .prproj reading, no embedded AAF/OMF audio extraction, and text/effect/mask/3D omissions or prerender needs. The string prproj resolves to FCP7 XML.
findings.risk: An extension/alias can create a misleading support claim and conceal non-editable or missing workflow data.
proposed_controls: Expose detected actual format, requested alias, conversion losses and source provenance.
Preserve full user native Adobe conversion scope in separate genuine format adapters.
Share one normalized media/timeline model across editing and compositing assets.
findings.proof_required: Original native project and interchange cases with missing effects, titles, audio, remaps, multicam and external references; NOT_RUN.

findings.title: Automation ingress and generic job spawning lack admission bounds
findings.observed: Automation uses a reader thread with .lines() and an unbounded std mpsc channel. Generic spawn_task starts a new thread and pushes into a task vector. Task state supports AtomicBool cancellation and Mutex progress/result; owner finish checks cancellation before applying a closure. No ingress bytes/items bound or thread admission bound exists in these inspected functions.
findings.risk: A fast or malformed swarm can accumulate input lines, queued jobs, threads, snapshots and result memory without a bounded overload outcome.
proposed_controls: Bound input line bytes, outstanding requests, queued/running jobs, snapshots and output receipts.
Use bounded actor inboxes and a budgeted worker pool with fair per-actor quotas.
Require job/actor/document/revision IDs and explicit accepted/overloaded/cancelled/completed receipts.
Keep mutation on one owner; parallelize immutable engine work and short local cache/budget synchronization.
findings.proof_required: Sustained overload, oversized lines, slow writer, stalled worker, cancellation storms, actor starvation and shutdown drain under byte/job budgets.

findings.title: A GPU pass count does not bound a stalled settle
findings.observed: Deferred render loops use MAX_PASSES=24 and await settle per pass; the inspected settle boundary has no cancel/deadline parameter. block_on polls with a noop waker and yield_now. Export separately uses callback cancellation and bounds Rayon worker count.
findings.risk: A hung GPU/driver pass can hold a job indefinitely; polling wastes CPU and ignores bounded job lifetime.
proposed_controls: Carry cancellation/deadline into GPU submission, settle and fallback.
Bound in-flight GPU resources and reserve bytes before work.
Expose adapter/backend/device loss/fallback and pressure state through Flight Recorder, internal diagnostics and Argus adapters.
findings.proof_required: Driver/device loss, unavailable adapter, delayed settle, concurrent export/preview and cancellation before/after submission.

findings.title: Render cache is a useful local dependency pattern, not CKC content authority
findings.observed: Pixel cache is an LRU guarded by a Mutex, with a 1 GiB default budget and an AtomicBool miss gate. Cache identity hashes project/footage versions, source/proxy/time, pipe/dimensions, layer switches, sampled property values and paint spans using an FNV hasher.
findings.risk: A version/local hash is not collision-resistant provenance or complete external-resource identity, and separate cache ownership can duplicate CKC budgets.
proposed_controls: Adapt dependency-key structure to shared CKC CAS and captured immutable resource content identities.
Keep expression, LUT, font, plugin and media dependencies explicit.
Bound active reservations plus retained cache bytes; do not count only LRU resident entries.
findings.proof_required: External resource replacement, hash collision handling, invalidation/replay, cache pressure and stale project/footage version tests.

findings.title: Wasm plugin limits are per instance rather than aggregate admission
findings.observed: The inspected plugin store limits memory to 1 GiB, instances to one and fuel to 50 million. Linker imports are rejected and API version checked. Idle instances are stored in a Mutex Vec; no aggregate pool or active-instance admission limit is visible in the inspected range.
findings.risk: Many allowed plugin instances can exceed process memory even when each respects its individual limit.
proposed_controls: Use one shared plugin resource budget with active/idle caps, reservation and cancellation.
Keep no ambient imports and explicit capability/version contracts.
Expose plugin identity, fuel/memory use and exhaustion as structured diagnostics.
findings.proof_required: Concurrent plugin pressure, idle-pool growth, fuel exhaustion, bad imports/API and cancellation.

findings.title: Menu implementation and internal CPU/GPU agreement do not prove After Effects parity
findings.observed: The menu stub registry returns an empty vector with a comment that menu entries are implemented. GPU tests compare internal CPU results, specify 8/high-depth tolerances and special discontinuity allowances, and skip when no adapter is available. An AE easing oracle script exists, but this lane did not inspect or execute it.
findings.risk: Broad feature labels and self-reference tests can conceal missing native semantics and independent visual differences.
proposed_controls: Use original-app workflow graphs and native input/output fixtures as independent acceptance surfaces.
Keep adapter/codec skips explicit.
Treat the uninspected AE oracle script as NOT_INSPECTED, not available proof.
findings.proof_required: Installed After Effects differential workflow/render/time/color/document tests; all NOT_RUN here.
